Cognex’s latest earnings call painted a decisively upbeat picture, as management balanced record results with measured caution on a few pockets of weakness. Executives emphasized broad-based demand, strong execution, and rising profitability, while describing headwinds in Europe, automotive, and components as manageable and already addressed by pricing and cost actions.
Record Revenue and Upgraded Growth Outlook
Cognex delivered a record quarterly revenue result, up 17% year-over-year, or 16% in constant currency, marking the eighth straight quarter of growth. Management’s confidence was clear as they lifted full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $1.13–1.15 billion, implying roughly 15% growth at the midpoint and closer to 16% excluding a prior one-time benefit.
Margin Expansion Drives Profit Upside
Profitability was a major bright spot, with adjusted EBITDA margin jumping to 32.2% in the quarter, a 1,150 basis-point improvement from a year ago and the eighth consecutive quarter of margin expansion. Adjusted gross margin also climbed 350 basis points to 71.5%, underscoring strong pricing power, mix, and operating discipline.
EPS Surge and Robust Free Cash Flow
Earnings power accelerated, as adjusted diluted EPS surged 80% year-over-year to $0.45 in the quarter, tracking well ahead of revenue growth and signaling strong operating leverage. Free cash flow rose about 70% to $68 million, and trailing 12-month free cash flow conversion reached 114%, extending a streak of more than 100% conversion to seven quarters.
Semiconductor and Logistics Lead End-Market Strength
Demand remained strong in key verticals, with semiconductor revenue growing at a double-digit rate across all regions and prompting management to raise its semiconductor outlook to double-digit growth for the full year. Electronics and packaging also posted double-digit gains, while logistics delivered its 10th straight quarter of double-digit growth, highlighting the diversity and resilience of Cognex’s end-market exposure.
China and Americas Power Geographic Growth
Growth was particularly strong in China, where revenue jumped 42% year-over-year and 40% year-to-date, confirming a robust recovery in that market. The Americas also showed impressive momentum with revenue up 27% year-over-year, supported by strength across end markets, and still posting double-digit growth even after adjusting for a procurement re-routing effect, while other parts of Asia grew 14%.
Expanding Customer Base and New Product Launches
Cognex continued to broaden its customer footprint, adding about 9,000 new customers in 2025 and roughly 4,500 more in the first part of 2026, which supports diversification and reduces dependence on any single industry. On the innovation front, the company highlighted OneVision and new In-sight products, including the 2800, L38, 3900, and 6900, aimed at expanding AI-enabled machine vision and unlocking new use cases.
Cost Discipline and Strong Operating Execution
Operating expenses moved in the right direction, with adjusted opex down 3% year-over-year and 5% in constant currency in the second quarter, showing tight cost control even as revenue grew. Management now expects about $35 million of annualized net cost reductions by the end of 2026 and noted that Q2 saw nearly 100% revenue flow-through to the bottom line, underscoring the power of the model.
Guidance Points to Continued Margin Gains
Cognex issued Q3 and full-year guidance that signals continued momentum, with Q3 revenue expected between $300 million and $320 million, or about 12% growth at the midpoint and closer to 17% excluding a prior one-time benefit. The company sees Q3 adjusted EBITDA margins of 32–35% and full-year margins of 29–31%, implying substantial year-over-year expansion, alongside sizable EPS growth and high flow-through on incremental revenue.
Europe Weakness and Automotive Soft Patch
Not all regions were firing, as Europe posted a 15% revenue decline year-over-year, though underlying performance was better, with only a low single-digit drop when adjusting for a procurement entity shift. Automotive was the main drag, with revenue down high single-digits in the quarter and roughly flat year-to-date, leading management to maintain a cautious full-year outlook of flat to low single-digit growth for that segment.
Component Costs and Portfolio Changes as Headwinds
Rising memory prices are creating some gross margin pressure, with management flagging about a 75 basis-point headwind in the third quarter and potential spillover into the fourth quarter, which they aim to offset with additional pricing actions. The company also reminded investors of portfolio optimization moves and timing effects, including revenue lost from divested non-core products and the impact of prior partnership and order timing shifts on year-over-year comparisons.
Visibility Limits, Macro Risks, and Seasonality
Management acknowledged that short-cycle visibility of roughly three to four months, along with broader macro and geopolitical risks, adds uncertainty around the outlook, despite the confidence expressed in issuing full-year guidance. The implied cadence points to a step-down in the fourth quarter versus the third, driven by typical seasonality, strong electronics growth earlier in the year, and tougher prior-year comparisons, leading the company to frame its stance as deliberately conservative.
Forward Guidance Signals Strong Growth with Built-In Caution
For the third quarter, Cognex projects revenue of $300–320 million, strong double-digit growth on an underlying basis, with adjusted EBITDA margins of 32–35% and a sharp step-up in EPS versus last year, even after factoring in memory cost pressures and portfolio headwinds. For full-year 2026, the company guides to mid-teens revenue growth, margin expansion of nearly nine percentage points at the midpoint, and EPS up more than 60%, all while incorporating cost savings, investment income, and known headwinds into its forecasts.
Cognex’s earnings call portrayed a company executing at a high level, with record sales, expanding margins, and powerful cash generation offsetting pockets of regional and sector softness. While management remains realistic about macro risks, component inflation, and seasonal patterns, the tone was confident, and the upgraded guidance suggests investors are being rewarded for staying patient through previous industry cycles.
